title: eval-harness: add CI hooks for prompt-set regression + quality gating
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Add lightweight CI hooks and a configurable gating layer that runs prompt-set regressions and quality metric checks on change. This PR introduces a new eval-ci job that runs a trimmed evaluation (sampled prompts + fast metrics) on affected prompt sets and model configs and fails the build if quality deltas exceed configured thresholds. The goal is to catch regressions early without requiring full nightly runs. Changes include: a new 'eval-ci' workflow, a gating library to compute deltas and apply thresholds, and decorators to mark prompt sets as 'fast' vs 'full'. The PR includes a checklist: 1) add eval-ci workflow, 2) implement gating logic and thresholds config, 3) wire up to existing metrics exporters, 4) update docs and README, 5) add unit + integration tests. Related: ENG-4821 (prompt gating design), ENG-4823 (fast eval runner). This description contains details about the behavior: the eval-ci job runs only when files under evaluations/prompts/ or harness/configs/ change, or when files in models/ are updated. The job runs on a sampled subset (configurable via environment variable SAMPLE_RATIO) and emits a concise JSON summary artifact with per-prompt and aggregate delta metrics. If any metric delta crosses a threshold defined in .eval-gates.yaml (per-prompt-set and per-metric), the job sets a status context 'eval/prompt-regression' to failure and adds a minimally formatted comment to the PR with the artifact link and offending prompt IDs. For maintainers, gates can be overridden by adding the label 'eval-gate:override' and a short justification in the PR body. The implementation aims to be conservative: default thresholds are permissive and the job is opt-in by adding an entry to .eval-gates.yaml or by touching a prompt set. Backwards compatibility: existing nightly/full evaluations are unchanged. See README changes for plugin usage and an example .eval-gates.yaml. CI behaviour: flakes are mitigated by a retry-on-failure wrapper for flaky model infra checks; the job is marked non-blocking when run in draft PRs. This PR includes tests that run the gating library against historical eval artifacts to validate delta computation and thresholding behavior.

review_comments: Diego Navarro: Please add an explicit timeout for the eval-ci job; we had long running jobs once in an earlier run.
Asha Patel: Added a 20m timeout and documented the environment variable to override for special cases.
Maya Chen: Gate thresholds look permissive — do we have a plan to tighten over time? Consider a scheduled job to propose threshold updates.
Asha Patel: Agreed; created ENG-4922 to track threshold tuning and added a note in docs about a monthly threshold review process.
Liam O'Connor: Could the job emit a condensed HTML/markdown report instead of raw JSON for quicker triage?

release_notes: Add fast eval CI workflow and gating library to detect prompt-set regressions in PRs; opt-in via .eval-gates.yaml; default thresholds are permissive.
